thread.title: Apple's Latest TV Team-Ups Highlight a Shifting Growth Strategy

title: Apple's Latest TV Team-Ups Highlight a Shifting Growth Strategy
text:
Apple’s Latest TV Team-Ups Highlight a Shifting Growth Strategy By Jan. 7, 2019 5:48 p.m. ET Order Reprints Courtesy of Samsung Text size
The road to growing Apple ’s (ticker: AAPL) increasingly important “ecosystem” might still run through devices—just not necessarily all Apple’s.
That became clear on Monday, when Samsung said it would offer Apple’s iTunes for movies and TV shows on its smart televisions—new ones starting later this year, and some older ones via update—as well as Apple’s AirPlay, which will let users stream from Apple devices to the television sets.
For Samsung, the announcement was part of several made at the 2019 Consumer Electronics Show.
The AirPlay announcement, meanwhile, was echoed by similar news on Monday from LG and Vizio about their own TVs. Newsletter Sign-up
Investor attention has been more focused on Apple than usual since last week, when it warned of weak iPhone sales in China and lowered its sales guidance for its December quarter . That has snowballed into a much broader re-evaluation of the outlook for its hardware and the speed with which it can become more of a services company collecting transactions or other fees.
CEO Tim Cook, in his recent letter to Apple shareholders , noted “services” as one of the categories that was growing as China iPhone sales slipped. And Apple followed that announcement with another in which it reported a “blockbuster” holiday for its App Store.
The intention, at least in part, was surely to reassure investors that its services business and marketplaces are healthy and growing.
Some of the conversations about what’s next at Apple have focused on physical goods, ranging from cars to television sets . Other times, such conversations have explored the possibility of Apple developing an Amazon.com -evoking (AMZN) Prime-like service bundle .
Earlier Monday, we wrote about a media analyst’s prediction that one of the “FAANG” companies might buy a videogame studio.
This latest set of announcements are a bit different, since they are about widening access to Apple services on different hardware—which, naturally, could affect demand for Apple’s own devices. Both the AirPlay and Samsung iTunes developments don’t exactly make the Apple TV a must-have.
This notion wasn’t invented today. In late November, for example, Amazon said Apple Music was coming to its Echo devices . It seems likely that we can expect more deals like this in 2019.
